fail_to_pass: RFC A.1 to A.5: add a member, add an array element, remove a member, remove an array element, replace a value
RFC A.6 and A.7: moving a value and moving an array element
RFC A.8 and A.9: a test that holds changes nothing, and one that does not hold fails
RFC A.10 to A.12: a nested object, unrecognised members are ignored, adding under a missing parent fails
RFC A.14 to A.16: escape order in pointers, a string is not a number, and appending an array
pointers: the empty pointer is the whole document, ~1 is a slash and ~0 a tilde, and a bad pointer is refused
array indexes: decimal digits with no leading zero, the end marker only for add, and no index past the end
add replaces an existing member; remove and replace need the target to exist
move: from must exist, equal paths do nothing, a path inside the source is refused
copy makes an independent copy
test compares by value: key order does not matter, arrays are ordered, types are not coerced
the document passed in is never changed, and the result shares nothing with it or with the patch
it is all or nothing: a failing operation leaves nothing applied and says which one failed
operations see the result of the ones before them
bad operations are refused: unknown or missing op, missing value, missing from, a patch that is not an array
a value of null is a value: it can be added, replaced and tested
keys named like object properties are ordinary keys and never reach a prototype
adds an object member
inserts into an array
a failed test operation is a PatchError that says which operation failed
